synthesis.procedure: Under argon (Schlenk/glovebox), CAN (548 mg, 1.00 mmol) was reacted with 5 equiv of Na(OCH2tBu) (551 mg, 5.00 mmol) in THF (8 mL) following the CAN protocol. After stirring 2 h at ambient temperature, centrifugation and evaporation of the supernatant gave a yellow-orange powder; extraction with toluene and solvent evaporation afforded crude [Ce(OCH2tBu)3(NO3)] (2) (427 mg, 0.92 mmol, 92%). Crystallization of crude 2 (360 mg, 0.78 mmol) from a toluene extract at −40 °C gave orange-red crystals of 3 suitable for X-ray diffraction. An alternative CAN run (CAN 181.1 mg, 0.33 mmol; 5.5 equiv Na(OCH2tBu) 200 mg, 1.82 mmol in THF 5 mL; 2 h ambient; toluene extraction overnight) also afforded putative crude 3 (103.5 mg, 0.05 mmol, 72%).

synthesis.procedure: Mixed-valent 4 formed as a decomposition product during attempted isolation of 2 and upon recrystallization of crystalline 3. Recrystallization of NMR-measured samples of 2 or 3 from toluene at −40 °C, and recrystallization of 3 from toluene at −40 °C, produced a slightly yellow precipitate within some days. Filtration left a luminous red solution from which red single crystals of 4 suitable for X-ray diffraction were grown (lattice toluene). No independent stoichiometric reagent amounts are given for the isolation of 4 itself.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtration of yellow precipitate; red crystals of 4 grown from the luminous red toluene solution; lattice toluene present.

properties.summary: 4 is mixed-valent (paramagnetic Ce(III) component). Crystalline 4 in toluene-d8 shows a wide 1H NMR window (δ 9.98 to −19.15 ppm). UV–vis of complexes 1–8 were recorded; 4 is a light-sensitive decomposition product. No numerical Evans χmol is given specifically for 4.

synthesis.procedure: Under argon, HOCH2tBu (45.5 mg, 0.52 mmol, 4 equiv) was added to [Ce{N(SiHMe2)2}4] (87.5 mg, 0.13 mmol) in n-hexane (5 mL). Instant color change from deep red to bright yellow. Evaporation of volatiles gave a yellow powder (crude yield >99%, 63.5 mg). Crystallization twice from concentrated n-hexane at −35 °C gave yellow crystals (23.5 mg, 0.04 mmol, 37%). Donor-free 6 sublimed virtually quantitatively at 150 °C under high vacuum (5 × 10−5 mbar) without significant decomposition.

properties.summary: Homoleptic Ce(IV) trimer 6 is light-sensitive. Evans method in C6D6 shows residual paramagnetism (χmol·T = 0.27 emu·K·mol−1; μeff = 1.46 μB). In toluene, a strong LMCT band at 295 nm has ε = 11421 L·mol−1·cm−1, higher than [Ce(OtBu)4(py)2] and 6(THF); onset of nitrate-free complexes is 400–450 nm.
